Maya: Heads up — after today's runtime merge (kernel-selector v2) we're seeing a big regression on multi-GPU TF serving jobs. All-reduce latency jumped ~2.5x and tail latency spiked. Tracked it down to comm/compute overlap lost during CUDA graph capture when KV prefetch is enabled.

Vikram: Can you paste the perf trace? which variant did the selector pick?

Maya: Here's a short perf snippet from the trace (nvprof/trace):
```
Timeline: stream0: compute (matmul_variant_A)
          stream1: kv_prefetch (hostMemcpyAsync -> hostSync)
          stream2: allreduce (nccl)
Observed: kv_prefetch introduces a host sync while graph capture active -> graph replay serializes streams -> nccl can't overlap with compute
Kernel chosen: matmul_fused_preload_sync (new heuristic picks it when seq_len>512)
```

Jules: ugh. "_fused_preload_sync_" sounds like the syncy path we added for preloading weights. Selector probably started preferring it because of latency microbench reweights.

Priya: Repro steps? is this across TPU/GPU or specific to A100 multi-socket?

Maya: Repro on A100 8x; also reproduced locally on 4x V100 with CUDA 11.8 + NCCL 2.14. Happens only when: (1) graph capture is enabled, (2) KV cache prefetching enabled, (3) kernel-selector picks the preload-sync variant.

Sam: Deploy bot: merge "runtime/kernel-selector-v2" -> prod completed 12:02 UTC :deploy: (build #4578)

Vikram: Two hypotheses: (A) kernel variant itself issues a host->device staging sync (bad), or (B) our prefetch path uses a blocking cudaMemcpyAsync/h2d that accidentally does a stream wait when captured into a CUDA graph.

Maya: I instrumented the capture with CUPTI markers — confirmed that the prefetch issues a host-side pinned memcpy with implicit host-sync in that kernel path. When captured, the CUDA graph serializes and later replay enqueues everything on the default stream ordering so NCCl can't overlap.

Jules: Quick mitigation options: disable KV prefetch during capture; or add a selector rule: prefer non-sync kernels when capture_flag=true; or change prefetch to use cudaMemcpyAsync on a non-captured stream with `cudaLaunchHostFunc` callback to avoid host-sync.

Priya: For customer impact we should flip the selector back to v1 for the next hotfix and ship a toggled config for KV prefetch off by default in capture scenarios. Which is fastest?

Vikram: Revert selector heuristics is fastest (one-liner revert), but I want a patch that prevents us regress again: add a capture-safety check to kernel-selector that forbids selecting _*_sync_* variants if `capture_enabled==true` or if `kv_prefetch==true` and `prefetch_mode==pinned`.

Maya: I'll produce a minimal reproducer and gprof timeline, attach the trace to the ticket. Also adding a temporary runtime flag `RDW_DISABLE_KV_PREFETCH_DURING_CAPTURE=true` we can flip in prod.

Sam: I'll open the revert PR now and coordinate a rollback window. InfraBot: schedule rollback slot?

InfraBot: autoserver: rollback window requested for runtime kernel-selector v2. Proposed window: 30m from now. Confirm with :ok_hand:.

Jules: One more thing — we should add a unit perf test: capture+prefetch+nccl overlap with synthetic model to detect future selector changes.

Priya: Agreed. Also add a perf alert on 95th percentile all-reduce latency for dedicated clusters.

Maya: Action items: (1) Maya -> repro + CUPTI trace -> ticket #INV-9421 (attached), (2) Sam -> revert PR and schedule rollback, (3) Vikram/Jules -> selector safe-guard patch, (4) Priya -> perf alert rule.

Vikram: I'm taking the selector patch. Will put up draft today.

Sam: Revert PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4682 (rolling back kernel-selector v2). TG for rollback at 12:45 UTC.

Priya: Thx everyone. We'll monitor after rollback and then ship safe-guard in a follow-up. :thumbsup:

Maya: I'll post the CUPTI traces and perf flamegraphs in the ticket shortly.

Jules: Nice triage. Low-risk rollback + a selector check seems solid.

Maya: FYI — temporary customer-facing mitigation: add run flag `--no-kv-prefetch` to the serving binary; doc note in release channel."
